statement_pretty:
∀ {X Y : SSet} (B : X.Subcomplex) (f : Y ⟶ X) {u : Set X.Subcomplex},
  u ⊂ lowerBounds (Set.Icc ((B.preimage f).image f) B) →
    ∀ {v w : Set X.Subcomplex},
      IsLUB (Set.Icc v u) w →
        Set.Ico v (Set.Iic ((B.preimage f).image f)) ⊆ Set.Icc v u →
          IsLUB (Set.Ico v (Set.Iic ((B.preimage f).image f))) w

Despite the simplicial set dressing, the argument reduces entirely to an elementary manipulation of intervals and cofinality in a partial order. The heavily contrived hypotheses on the sets u, v, and w render this a minor technical lemma of negligible independent interest.

editorial.title: The Simplicial Subcomplex Interval-Supremum Lemma

editorial.unverified_gloss:
For any morphism `f : Y ⟶ X` of simplicial sets and subcomplex `B` of `X`, let `I = f(f⁻¹(B))` be the image of the preimage of `B` (which satisfies `I ≤ B`). Working in the poset of sets of subcomplexes of `X` ordered by inclusion, if `u` is a proper subset of the lower bounds of `[I, B]` (i.e., `u ⊂ {S | S ≤ I}`) and `w` is the least upper bound of `[v, u]`, then `w` is also the least upper bound of the half-open interval `[v, {S | S ≤ I})`, provided `[v, {S | S ≤ I}) ⊆ [v, u]`.

The simplicial set setup is largely decorative: since `I ≤ B` forces the lower bounds of `[I, B]` to be `{S | S ≤ I}`, the strict inclusion `u ⊂ {S | S ≤ I}` puts `[v, u]` inside `[v, {S | S ≤ I})`, and the assumed reverse inclusion makes the two intervals cofinal (in fact equal), so they share the same least upper bound `w`.
